title: Crossing the road safely
examples: What should I do before I walk into the street?
Where is the safest place to cross the road?
Do I need an adult to cross the road?

explain.say: Always stop at the edge of the pavement before you cross.
Next, look all around for traffic. Look both ways.
Then listen carefully for cars and bikes.
Use a crossing place, like a zebra crossing, when there is one.
Always hold a grown-up's hand when you cross.
Walk straight across. Keep looking and listening as you walk.

faq.q: What is the first thing I must do before I cross?
faq.a: You must always stop at the edge of the pavement first. This keeps you safe until you are ready to go.

faq.q: How do I know if it is safe to cross?
faq.a: Look all around and listen for traffic. Cross with a grown-up when the road is clear.
asks: Is it safe to cross now?
What should I check before walking out?

faq.q: Where is the best place to cross the street?
faq.a: The best places are crossings, like zebra crossings or traffic lights. A grown-up can help you choose.
asks: What are the safe crossing spots?

faq.q: Why should I hold an adult's hand?
faq.a: Holding an adult's hand keeps you close and safe from cars. Grown-ups know the rules very well.

faq.q: What if I hear a car coming?
faq.a: Wait at the kerb with your grown-up. Cross only when it is safe.
asks: What do I do if I hear a noise?

facts: Always stop at the kerb before crossing.
Look all around for traffic, and listen too.
Use crossings like zebra crossings or traffic lights.
Hold a grown-up's hand for extra safety.

quiz.say: You come to the edge of the road. What do you do first?
quiz.why: Stopping at the kerb gives you time to look and listen.

wrong.1: Running into the road is unsafe, so stop first.
wrong.2: A ball in the road is a job for a grown-up, so stop and tell them.

quiz.say: You are at a zebra crossing with a grown-up. What do you do?
quiz.why: Wait until the cars have stopped. Then walk across with your grown-up.

wrong.0: Cars need time to stop, so wait at the kerb.
wrong.2: Running can make you trip, so walk across.

quiz.say: Which steps keep you safe, in the right order?
quiz.why: Stop at the kerb, then look and listen. Cross only when it is safe.

wrong.0: Crossing first is unsafe, so stop and check before you go.
wrong.1: Stopping comes before crossing, at the kerb.
